topic: Running .ts files in Node: type stripping fails on enums, so use erasableSyntaxOnly and as const objects
text:
Node can run .ts files directly now. But an enum in that file will crash it.

Node's built-in type stripping only erases types, replacing them with whitespace. It never generates JavaScript, so anything that needs generated code fails. Per the Node docs, that includes:

• enum declarations
• namespaces with runtime code (ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX)
• constructor parameter properties
• import aliases

TypeScript 5.8 added erasableSyntaxOnly, so the compiler flags these before Node does. Node also does no type checking, so keep tsc --noEmit in CI.

My rule: new code gets an as const object plus a union type instead of an enum. Same autocomplete, nothing to generate.

If you've moved a codebase off enums, what was the hardest part to replace?
